records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result's 'advanced feature' branch executes queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset = cursor.offset taken straight from the client-controlled cursor value, so any negative offset in a crafted cursor is handed to Django slicing unvalidated. A client sending a cursor with a negative offset to the audit-log endpoint with optimized_pagination=true gets a 500 (ValueError from the ORM's negative-slice guard) or, where executed, rows anchored to the end of the table rather than the cursor position — repeated page traversal under this paginator returns duplicated/misordered audit rows with no error surfaced.
records.rationale: The diff adds an explicit negative-slice path in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`: `if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0: start_offset = cursor.offset ... results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` (new code in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`). Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative indices, so this path will raise at runtime for crafted cursors, yielding a 500. The code comment claims “The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically”, but the implementation still performs a negative slice bound, matching the finding’s failure mode.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The prev-page boundary trimming in OptimizedCursorPaginator compares len(results) == offset + limit + extra against a possibly-negative offset, so the trim condition can never match or matches spuriously, leaving the duplicate boundary row in the prev page. Administrators paging backwards through audit logs with the optimized paginator receive a duplicated row at each page boundary (the row already shown as the last item of the previous page), corrupting the client's view of the audit trail with no indication anything was skipped or repeated.
records.rationale: The described mismatch can’t occur in the code shown because the trimming logic only runs under `if cursor.is_prev and cursor.value:` and in that case `start_offset` is explicitly set to `offset` (not a clamped value): `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. Therefore `results` is sliced from `start_offset == offset`, so `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` is not comparing against a different offset due to `start_offset != offset` in the prev-cursor branch.

When an is_prev cursor carries a negative offset, the duplicated boundary row is silently returned to the client as part of a 200 response — data silently duplicated with no error surfaced, corrupting the client's pagination view.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The base paginator's rewritten slicing `max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` silently diverges from the OptimizedCursorPaginator's semantics for prev cursors, keeping negative offsets unclamped on the shared path used by every DateTimePaginator endpoint. Any existing endpoint whose client crafts a prev cursor with a negative offset now reaches queryset[negative:stop] on the shared BasePaginator path and gets a 500 where the previous code computed stop identically — the conditional clamping makes the two paginators' boundary behavior inconsistent and future maintainers can't reason about which applies where.
